writeup.headline: Addus HomeCare rates Hold at 63, two points short of Buy, on solid valuation and trend scores.
writeup.thesis: Addus scores 63, a Hold that sits 2 points below the Buy edge at 65. Valuation (76) is the strongest factor: at 1.5x sales, 14.7x free cash flow and 16.1x EV/EBIT, with an FCF yield 1.8 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield, the shares look moderate in absolute terms, and they are cheap against their own history, with P/FCF cheaper than at 46 of the last 61 month-ends. The balance sheet (74) is sound with net debt at 0.66 times free cash flow, and the trend (71) is strong, with the price 0.5% below its 52-week high and the shares 16.9 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Growth (55) and quality (56) hold the score back: TTM revenue growth of 15.9% contrasts with latest-quarter revenue growth of 8.0% year on year, and margins are modest, with a 32.4% gross margin and a 10.0% operating margin. News is neutral (50), with the pending AccentCare acquisition and Q3 results on 2026-11-03 the next catalysts.
key_risks: Q3 results on 2026-11-03 could disappoint against the FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 12–13%.
AccentCare acquisition still awaits regulatory approval and carries integration risk.
Heavy reliance on government and managed care payers, with Illinois and Texas the largest markets, exposes the company to reimbursement changes.
Latest-quarter revenue growth of 8.0% is well below TTM revenue growth of 15.9%, suggesting slowing momentum.
Barclays reiterated Underweight with a $96 target, and earlier BofA and Citi downgrades show analyst skepticism.
what_would_change: A 2-point gain, for example from stronger Q3 growth lifting the growth score or margin improvement lifting quality, would move the rating to Buy.
Positive guidance or a clean AccentCare approval could raise the news score from its neutral 50 and push the total past 65.
A fall of 19 points would be needed for Sell, such as a sharp price reversal hurting trend combined with weak results or negative news.
